title: What is the smallest number with remainders two, three and four?
description: A number leaves remainder two on division by three, three on division by four, and four on division by five. The video notices that each remainder is one short of its divisor, adds one, and uses the smallest number all three divide.
teaching_notes: One idea: when every remainder is one short of its divisor, adding one makes the number a multiple of all the divisors. Watch for students who list numbers one by one and never explain why the first one found is the smallest.

source: Figure it Out (multiples and remainders, question 8)
video_script.why: The student can find numbers with a common remainder on two divisors and now meets remainders that differ but are each one short of the divisor.
video_script.substitution: Add one to the number so every remainder becomes a full group, then use the smallest number that three, four and five all divide.
video_script.anchor: dots in groups of three, four and five, each group one dot short of full
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest number is fifty nine

final_answer.value: 59; it is the smallest because 60 is the smallest common multiple of 3, 4 and 5
final_answer.spoken: fifty nine, because sixty is the smallest common multiple of three, four and five

maths_rules: remainders 2, 3, 4 are each 1 less than the divisors 3, 4, 5, so n + 1 is a multiple of 3, 4 and 5
numbers both 4 and 5 divide: 20, 40, 60; only 60 is also a multiple of 3
least common multiple of 3, 4 and 5 is 60, so the smallest n + 1 is 60 and n = 59
every common multiple is 60 or more, so n + 1 cannot be less than 60
video_script.design: Dots in groups of three, four and five, each one dot short. One dot is added to complete every group, then taken away again at the end.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: add 1: 2 + 1 = 3, 3 + 1 = 4, 4 + 1 = 5; n + 1 is a multiple of 3, of 4 and of 5

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, add one to the number. Two and one make three, three and one make four, and four and one make five.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>The number n plus one is a multiple of three, of four and of five.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 4 and 5 both divide 20, 40, 60; 3 divides 60 only; least common multiple = 60

marks.find: the words smallest number that 3, 4 and 5 all divide appear

marks.twenty: twenty, forty and sixty are written as numbers that four and five both divide
marks.sixty: sixty is ticked for three, and twenty and forty are crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>Step two, find the smallest number that three, four and five all divide.
<bookmark mark='name'/>This number is called the least common multiple.
<bookmark mark='twenty'/>Numbers that four and five both divide are twenty, forty, sixty and so on.
<bookmark mark='sixty'/>Three divides sixty but not twenty or forty. The least common multiple is sixty.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: n + 1 = 60, so n = 60 - 1 = 59; every common multiple is 60 or more, so n + 1 cannot be less than 60

marks.take: one is taken away from sixty
marks.why: the words every common multiple is 60 or more appear

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step three, the smallest n plus one is sixty. Take the one away, and the number is fifty nine.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Every common multiple is sixty or more, so n plus one cannot be less than sixty.

<bookmark mark='fours'/>It is four times fourteen plus three.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 59; it is the smallest because 60 is the smallest common multiple of 3, 4 and 5
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The smallest number is fifty nine.
It is the smallest because sixty is the smallest common multiple of three, four and five.
